title: Planetary Nebula Abell 74
caption: The planetary nebula Abell 74, imaged by the Mayall 4-meter Telescope
credit: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA)

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: Abell 74, in the constellation Vulpecula, is an ancient planetary nebula, and its great age makes it a very faint target to observe.
A planetary nebula is the shell of gas thrown off by a dying Sun-like star. Over time, the shell expands and thins out, and it grows dimmer as it spreads further from the star that lights it.

Old planetary nebulae are often bent out of shape, because as they drift through space they collide with the interstellar medium, the thin gas between the stars. Abell 74 is unusual because it has stayed highly symmetric in spite of its age. It seems to have kept its round shape where many others of its age have been distorted by their surroundings.

understand.summary: The Mayall 4-meter Telescope's Mosaic camera used two narrowband filters. Hydrogen-alpha is shown in red and oxygen [O III] in blue.
filters: 499 nm · Optical Olll (NSF Nicholas U. Mayall 4-meter Telescope Mosaic I)
656 nm · Optical Ha (NSF Nicholas U. Mayall 4-meter Telescope Mosaic I)
understand.eye: The nebula is too faint for the eye. Narrow filters and long exposures bring out its glow.
